answer: Prover samples pseudo-random RAM offsets along a timber-sealed walk, reading fixed-stride cache lines in strict physical order, then cryptographically closes the sequence into a root hash. Verifier replays one random inlet slice of that walk; a forged identity cannot fake contiguous DRAM latency below 20ns at each nadir offset. Each identity burns 64 GB of sealed RAM for 6 hours, costing roughly $90 per join—so farming 5000 fake agents demands $450000 and real silicon.
